item.title: Ripple effects: After Hearn, three others have their Reflecting Pool charges dropped
item.description: Prosecutors dropped their case against David Hearn on Friday, blaming Reflecting Pool damage on a "botched installation" rather than vandalism. That has implications for other people who were charged.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: With U.S. doors shutting, Cubans turn to Brazil for asylum
item.description: For years, many Cubans hoping to leave the island looked to the United States. Now, with legal pathways largely closed, a growing number are heading to Brazil instead.
item.content:encoded:

(Image credit: Ramon Espinosa)

item.title: Two people in Michigan have died after becoming ill with cyclosporiasis
item.description: They are the first reported deaths linked to a massive outbreak of the intestinal illness that began in May.

item.title: U.S. men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino will stay through 2030 World Cup
item.description: Pochettino came on in 2024 to right the ship ahead of this year's World Cup, in which he led the team to a record three wins and helped ignite enthusiasm in millions of fans before a round of 16 exit.

item.description: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche rescinds President Trump's anti-weaponization fund ahead of his confirmation hearing. And, the president calls off strikes on Iran over a potential deal.

item.title: What would it take to get peptides on the shelf?
item.description: An FDA advisory panel recently voted to green-light some popular peptides. The decision brought enormous attention to the market for these products — and concerns about the unregulated supply.

item.title: For those with criminal records, AI is breaking down barriers to employment
item.description: Tens of millions of Americans have criminal records that can be barriers to employment. An AI-powered app is helping those eligible to expunge their records at a pace not seen before.

item.title: Rare photos of ex-Myanmar leader Aung San Suu Kyi give her family hope
item.description: Kim Aris, son of Aung San Suu Kyi, told NPR that photographs of his mother meeting a foreign official gave him "a reason to hope" for the first time since the military coup that ousted her in 2021.
